story.title: Kushner Engages in Middle East Talks to Revive Gaza Peace Plan Amid Israeli Resistance
story.summary: Jared Kushner, the US envoy, is on a diplomatic mission in the Middle East, meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Hamas officials to revive a stalled peace plan for Gaza. This effort follows Netanyahu's recent rejection of a US-backed 15-point peace plan, marking a significant divergence from the Trump administration's approach. Kushner indicated that progress towards disarming Hamas could potentially begin within 30 days.

timeline_highlights.summary: President Trump has announced a deal for Hamas to completely disarm, which includes the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. However, the implementation of this deal is contingent upon Israel fulfilling its commitments from a previous agreement.

timeline_highlights.summary: Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks against Russia, targeting Moscow and nearby areas, which resulted in at least six fatalities. The strikes also hit a warehouse linked to a major online retailer. Concurrently, drone and missile strikes across both Russia and Ukraine led to additional civilian casualties, with reports indicating a total of at least 19 deaths from the combined attacks over the weekend.

event_overview.title: About Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.subject: Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.summary: The Gaza Peace Deal refers to the U.S.-backed, internationally supported framework to end the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza through a ceasefire, hostage and detainee releases, Hamas’s disarmament and Gaza’s demilitarization, Israeli withdrawals tied to agreed milestones, humanitarian access, and postwar governance and reconstruction. It builds on earlier Egypt-, Qatar-, and U.S.-mediated ceasefire efforts, but its implementation depends on compliance and verification by multiple parties rather than on a single self-executing agreement.

facts.label: Framework and international status
facts.value: President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan is a 20-point roadmap; the United Nations Security Council endorsed the plan in Resolution 2803 (2025) and welcomed a Board of Peace to support its implementation.

facts.label: Core proposed exchange and military step
facts.value: The framework envisages an end to military operations and a staged Israeli withdrawal, alongside the return of hostages and the release of specified Palestinian detainees; further withdrawal is linked to agreed demilitarization standards, milestones, and timeframes.

facts.label: Disarmament and transitional governance
facts.value: A subsequent 15-point implementation roadmap, presented by Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, the United States, and the High Representative for Gaza, calls for Hamas to end military, policing, and administrative activity and for the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) to serve as the transitional civilian authority.

facts.label: Institutions and outside roles
facts.value: The plan’s implementation architecture includes the Board of Peace, an Office of the High Representative for Gaza, the NCAG, and an International Stabilization Force intended to support security, demilitarization, aid delivery, and reconstruction. Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, and the United States are identified as guarantors in the UN implementation report.

facts.label: Legal and humanitarian context
facts.value: The International Committee of the Red Cross considers Gaza occupied territory under its effective-control assessment and states that international humanitarian law continues to govern protections for civilians and duties relevant to the territory’s administration and supply.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows reported late-July to mid-August 2026 developments concerning the deal’s implementation, Israeli-Hamas military and political responses, and one related Lebanon escalation; it is not a complete chronology of the Gaza war, all negotiations, humanitarian conditions, or the wider regional conflict.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed after Kushner's talks?
explore_lenses.title: No Israeli commitment, but a possible shift in sequencing
explore_lenses.summary: Kushner's August 17 meeting with Netanyahu did not produce Israel’s acceptance of the 15-point roadmap. However, U.S. negotiators appeared to accept Israel’s insistence that Hamas disarmament precede reconstruction, which would alter the roadmap’s reciprocal, phased structure.

claims.text: The Kushner-Netanyahu meeting ended without a concrete Israeli commitment to the U.S.-proposed roadmap; Israel also did not publicly commit to withdrawing from the roughly 60% of Gaza then controlled by its forces.

AP reported that U.S. negotiators appeared to accept Israel’s demand that Hamas disarm before reconstruction begins, while the published roadmap pairs phased weapons decommissioning with corresponding Israeli and other stakeholder steps.

The reported 30-day prospect is not a binding implementation deadline in the published roadmap: its stated procedural deadline is 14 days to prepare a timetable and mechanisms, and that clock starts only after all parties approve the roadmap.

explore_lenses.label: Why are Netanyahu and Hamas at odds over timing?
explore_lenses.title: Both sides endorse disarmament in principle, but dispute conditions
explore_lenses.summary: The central dispute is sequencing and verification, not simply whether Gaza should be demilitarized. Netanyahu says Israel cannot withdraw before complete disarmament; Hamas says implementation requires an Israeli halt to attacks and withdrawal toward the preexisting dividing line.

claims.text: Netanyahu’s position is that Israel will not withdraw from its Gaza positions until Hamas has been completely disarmed.

A Hamas official told AP that the group was committed to the roadmap but wanted mediators to begin the conditional 14-day planning period; the official also demanded that Israel halt attacks and withdraw to the so-called yellow line before implementation.

The roadmap calls for international verification, transfer of weapons to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, and an International Stabilization Force to support weapons custody and separate Israeli forces from committee-controlled areas.

Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Pakistan, and Indonesia argued in a joint foreign-ministers statement that Israel’s rejection was obstructing peace efforts and urged the United States and Board of Peace to prevent obstruction by any party.

explore_lenses.label: What would happen next if the roadmap is approved?
explore_lenses.title: A conditional transition to technocratic Gaza governance
explore_lenses.summary: Approval would begin a short planning phase rather than immediate full implementation. The intended end state is civilian administration by a Palestinian technocratic committee, internationally verified demilitarization, phased Israeli withdrawal, and then reconstruction.

claims.text: Once all parties approve the roadmap, they are to prepare an implementation timetable and mechanisms within 14 days; an International Verification Committee can extend that period and must certify compliance before Phase 2 proceeds.

After the timetable is completed, the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza is supposed to enter Gaza and assume civilian responsibilities; Hamas and other factions are to relinquish civilian governance and security functions.

The roadmap envisions weapons being decommissioned and stored under the committee’s authority, with militia members excluded from security and police services; Israeli forces would then complete a phased withdrawal on an agreed timetable.
Forecast: AP reported that reconstruction and deployment of international forces would remain on hold if the disarmament-withdrawal dispute persists.

story_report.summary: Jared Kushner has met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Hamas officials in an effort to revive a U.S.-backed Gaza roadmap after Netanyahu rejected it earlier this month. Kushner said Hamas disarmament could begin within 30 days, but the meeting produced no concrete Israeli commitment and no publicly agreed sequence for disarmament, Israeli withdrawal, reconstruction or verification.

sections.heading: Disarmament and Withdrawal Remain Divisive
sections.body: Netanyahu’s stated position is that Israeli forces will not withdraw from their Gaza positions until Hamas is completely disarmed. A Hamas official told AP that the group was committed to the roadmap, but said Israel must halt attacks and withdraw to the so-called yellow line before implementation. Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Pakistan and Indonesia said Israel’s rejection was obstructing peace efforts and urged the United States and Board of Peace to prevent obstruction by any party.

sections.heading: Roadmap Sets Conditional Implementation Process
sections.body: The published roadmap requires all parties to approve it before a 14-day period begins to prepare an implementation timetable and mechanisms; an International Verification Committee may extend the period and must certify compliance before Phase 2. The plan calls for Hamas and other factions to relinquish civilian governance and security duties, weapons to be placed under the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, and an International Stabilization Force to support weapons custody and separation of Israeli forces from committee-controlled areas. Israeli forces would then complete a phased withdrawal on an agreed timetable.

sections.heading: Stalemate Risks Delaying Reconstruction Plans
sections.body: U.S. negotiators appeared to accept Israel’s demand that Hamas disarm before reconstruction begins, although the published roadmap pairs phased weapons decommissioning with corresponding Israeli and other stakeholder steps. AP reported that reconstruction and deployment of international forces would remain on hold if the dispute over disarmament and withdrawal continues. No agreed timetable had been announced as of Aug. 18, and the technocratic committee had not entered Gaza.

unresolved.text: The parties have not publicly agreed on what constitutes complete or sufficiently verified Hamas disarmament, or whether Israel would accept a phased withdrawal before that threshold is met.

related_stories.title: Murder Trial for Tupac Shakur Opens 30 Years After His Death
related_stories.summary: The murder trial for Tupac Shakur has commenced nearly 30 years after the rapper was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas. Prosecutors allege that a former street gang leader, known as 'Keffe D,' orchestrated the attack as an act of revenge for the beating of his nephew. The trial marks a significant development in a case that has long been considered one of the most prominent cold cases in the U.S.
